bullets.title: NVDA Q2 Beat: $96.2B Revenue, 70% FY28 Growth Guide; Gross Margin Step-Down Key Risk
bullets.body: NVDA reported Q2 revenue of $96.2B (vs. $92.3B consensus) and EPS of $2.22 (vs. $2.09); Q3 guided to $108B (vs. $104.9B Street). CEO Jensen Huang cited accelerating AI demand with multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel. The key negative: Q3 gross margin guided at 74% (vs. 75% LT target) due to Vera Rubin ramp costs. Citi maintains Buy at $300 PT (~24x C27E). Hedgeye flagged FCF of only $21.4B vs. $47.2B Bloomberg estimate, a jump in DSOs, and strategic commitments surging from $119B to $279B (primarily memory procurement). Stock initially fell 3% post-report before recovering to +4-5% on the 70% FY28 revenue growth guide.

bullets.title: NVDA/AMZN: AWS Expands Strategic Collaboration, 2M GPU Deployment Planned 2027-2028
bullets.body: AWS and NVIDIA announced a major expansion of their strategic partnership, including deployment of 2M additional NVIDIA GPUs across AWS global infrastructure in 2027-2028, building AI factories for U.S. government with 100,000 GPUs on secure AWS infrastructure, and Amazon Robotics adopting NVIDIA physical AI for warehouse automation. NVIDIA Vera CPU-based infrastructure also coming to AWS.

bullets.title: CRM Surges ~13% AH: Claudeforce Partnership with Anthropic, AI ARR Approaching $4B
bullets.body: Salesforce Q2 EPS of $5.90 crushed the $3.27 FactSet consensus; FY27 EPS guidance raised to $16.67-16.71 from $14.06-14.12 (+18%). cRPO grew 13.9% and NNAOV growth was the strongest in four years. The headline catalyst was the Claudeforce partnership with Anthropic integrating Claude AI into Salesforce's enterprise platform with 37 prebuilt sales skills. AI and data products ARR is approaching $4B. Jefferies called this the best EPS move for CRM in ~6 years.

bullets.title: CRWD Q2 Beat: Net New ARR $333M vs. $310M Expected; Raises FY27 ARR Growth to 34%
bullets.body: CrowdStrike delivered Q2 revenue of $1.47B (vs. $1.44B consensus), EPS $0.31 (vs. $0.29), and net new ARR of $332.8M well above the $285-310M bogey. Management raised FY27 net new ARR growth guidance to 34% at midpoint and noted a record Q3 pipeline. Stock traded +9.5-11% after-hours.

bullets.title: MRVL: Earnings Aug 27, Buyside Expects 15% QoQ Revenue Growth; AI ASIC Business Could Hit $4B in F28
bullets.body: JPM notes MRVL reports tomorrow with buyside survey showing 15% sequential revenue growth expectations. The AI custom ASIC business is expected to more than double to $4B in F28, with the Google partnership described as 'transformational at $20B p.a. implied business.' MRVL trades at 35x F28 EPS vs. AVGO and NVDA in the teens, with positioning score of 1 (light).

bullets.title: META: $16.68B Settlement with 48 States on Teen Safety; $10B Q3 Legal Accrual
bullets.body: Meta reached a settlement with 48 state AGs for up to $16.68B payable over 10 years, resolving teen social-media addiction claims. The company will accrue ~$10B in legal expenses in Q3. The settlement includes default 2-hour daily limits for teens, restrictions on late-night access, and prohibition on using under-13 data for ad targeting. Section 230 shielded core platform features. Evercore reiterated Outperform at $860 PT on reduced legal risk; the larger residual risk is thousands of personal injury plaintiffs with state court trials beginning late October. Stock opened +4% to premarket high then reversed.

bullets.title: INTU Downgraded at Wolfe and JPMorgan; Weak Tax Segment Guide Drives Cuts
bullets.body: Intuit reported an F4Q26 beat but guided FY27 revenue to ~9% growth vs. consensus 11%, with the Tax segment guided at just +2% Y/Y. Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform (from Outperform) and JPMorgan also downgraded to Neutral. Three-year consumer segment CAGR target of 4-8% viewed as weak. Stock -3.8% mid-session.

bullets.title: SNPS Q3 Beat and FY Raise; After-Hours Sell-Off Seen as Overdone
bullets.body: Synopsys reported Q3 revenue of $2.48B (+42% YoY) and EPS of $3.91-4.10 (vs. $3.67-3.68 consensus), raising FY26 revenue guide to $9.71B and EPS midpoint to $15.07. Mizuho (Outperform, $600 PT) and Morgan Stanley (Equal-weight, $500 PT) both commented; Mizuho called the after-hours sell-off overdone. Investors focused on Agentic EDA offerings (AgentEngineer). Restructuring charges raised to $425-500M from $300-350M following ANSYS integration.

bullets.title: CDNS: 10-15 Year Runway from Custom Chip Design, AI Automation; $8.1B Backlog
bullets.body: At the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, Cadence highlighted above-market growth drivers including more systems companies designing custom chips, AI 'super agents' automating chip design, and customer R&D budgets shifting toward software. IP business targeting ~$1B annual run rate by year-end. Record $8.1B backlog provides forward visibility; China expected to grow at least in-line with company average.

bullets.title: INTC: 14A on Track, Advanced Packaging Could Hit $40% Margins; Data-Center CPU Demand Strengthening
bullets.body: Intel at Deutsche Bank Tech Conference indicated 14A risk production in 2027 and HVM in 2028, with advanced packaging expected to become a multibillion-dollar-per-customer business at ~40% gross margins by 2028-2029. Data-center CPU demand is strengthening sharply from AI inference and agentic workloads; supply, not competitiveness, is the main constraint through 2027-2028. Foundry break-even targeted end of 2027.

bullets.title: ORCL Added to Citi's 90-Day Catalyst Watch; Buy Rating, $330 PT
bullets.body: Oracle was added to Citi's upside 90-Day Catalyst Watch with a Buy rating and $330 price target. At Deutsche Bank Tech Conference, Oracle highlighted deferred revenue outpacing in-period revenue (strong forward bookings), cloud database growth with 22 new multi-cloud regions including Amazon, and AI-driven tools reducing ERP go-live times from years to months.

bullets.title: SMCI: TD Cowen Reiterates Buy/Top Pick, Raises FY28 EPS to $5.65 on 120% DC Growth
bullets.body: TD Cowen reiterated Buy and Top Pick designation on SMCI, raising its price target to $215 and lifting FY28 EPS estimate by 68% to $5.65 (vs. consensus $3.82). FY27 Data Center growth now modeled at +120% (previously ~85%), with 50% allocated to 1.6T Trainium/Inferentia AI accelerators.

bullets.title: WSM: KeyBanc Raises PT to $270 on Strong 2Q Share Gains; AI Assistants Driving 3x Conversion
bullets.body: Williams-Sonoma delivered the strongest 2Q sales in four years with all brands posting positive comps. AI assistants (Olive at Williams-Sonoma, Otto at Pottery Barn) are driving 3x higher conversion rates and 9x revenue per visit. Company raised FY26 guidance to 4.7-7.2% top-line growth. KeyBanc raised PT from $250 to $270 and reiterated Overweight.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Event Set for September 9; IDC Forecasts 10M Foldable iPhones Year 1
bullets.body: Apple sent invites for an iPhone 18 launch event on September 9th at 1PM ET. IDC separately projects Apple will sell 10 million foldable iPhones in the first year of availability.

bullets.title: AMD: 'Higher Low' Pattern Forming; AMD Presents Physical AI Architecture at Hot Chips 2026
bullets.body: AMD is displaying a bullish 'higher low' technical pattern per one commentator. At Hot Chips 2026, AMD presented its secure computing adaptive SOC architecture targeting physical AI, data center, and mission-critical systems applications.

bullets.title: VRT +3%: Industrials Outperform on AI/DC Exposure; OKLO, SMR, NNE Under Pressure
bullets.body: S&P 1500 Industrials gained 1.06% vs. S&P -0.02%, led by Electricals +2.3% with VRT +3% on AI/data center exposure. Nuclear power names OKLO -6.0%, SMR -5.5%, and NNE -3.8% fell on sector headwinds per the Industrials and Power sector summaries.

bullets.title: LITE Highlighted as High-Quality AI Infrastructure Play as Bottleneck Trade Rotates
bullets.body: With the AI bottleneck trade deemed over per the Gavin Baker thesis, market participants are now discriminating between low and high-quality AI names. LITE was noted as the 2025 consensus winner at the Jefferies semis conference and continues to show upward trajectory as a high-quality AI infrastructure play. Jefferies LOs also prefer memory names (SNDK) over semicaps.

bullets.title: MU: TSM Former Chairman's $8M Insider Buy Now Up 177%; New COO/President Named
bullets.body: Social media noted that TSMC's former chairman bought $8M of Micron at all-time highs, and MU is now up 177% since that purchase—cited as a demonstration of insider conviction. Separately, Micron named Manish Bhatia as COO and President.

bullets.title: NVDA CUDA Moat Under Pressure: OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC and Tensordyne Auto-Kernel Generation
bullets.body: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC claims a performance edge over NVIDIA's GB300 (noting HBM4 vs. HBM3E memory generation gap). Separately, Tensordyne claims agentic AI can now auto-generate GPU kernels, potentially eroding CUDA's software moat for inference workloads. Meta's MTIA 300 and Google's TPU v10 also advancing the custom silicon race. Jefferies noted OpenAI's custom chip could pressure NVDA dominance and inference margins.

bullets.title: APP PT Cut to $475 by Needham; CHTR PT Cut to $37 by Morgan Stanley; AFRM PT Raised to $80
bullets.body: Needham cut APP price target to $475 from $500. Morgan Stanley cut CHTR price target to $37 from $42. Morgan Stanley raised AFRM price target modestly to $80 from $79.
